newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Harmony eyes West Africa exploration.
newsitem.headline: Harmony eyes West Africa exploration.

text.p: Harmony Gold Mining Co Ltd could soon move into exploration and development in West Africa, managing director Bernard Swanepoel said on Monday.
"West Africa will offer interesting opportunities to Harmony in the near future," he said at a presentation of mine manager Randgold and Exploration Co Ltd second quarter gold results.
Swanepoel said that Harmony's recent acquisition of Lydenburg Exploration Ltd (Lydex) had won for it assets, including prospecting permits in West Africa, particularly in Ghana.
Lydex was delisted from the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in March, 1997.
Randgold's seven gold mines together made a pre-capex cash loss of 40.95 million rand for the second quarter compared to a 54.99 million rand profit in the preceding quarter.
Steady performer Harmony made a pre-capex cash profit in the quarter of 35.16 million rand from 39.59 million rand previously, increasing gold output to 5,543 kg from 5,479 kg.
